title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a baseline single‑shot LLM configuration generator against a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline (with a canary stage) on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2000 paired episodes). The declared model was gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses) and validation used a deterministic digital‑twin validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Under preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics exactly one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by both arms; downstream validation and the permitted single repair call (guarded arm only) were the only mechanisms for paired outcome differences. Observed outcomes: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). The preregistered primary inferential test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered secondary descriptive summary (paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI, 10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.001, 0.01]. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We report the exact McNemar result as the preregistered confirmatory outcome, present the bootstrap CI as a secondary descriptive summary, explicitly label a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) as exploratory/post‑hoc (it was not specified in the frozen preregistration), and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, high baseline validity, validator scope, and the shared_initial_candidate design.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation for network operations offers operational leverage but creates safety risks: multi‑step sequencing errors, transient invariant violations, and protected‑field interference can convert plausible command sequences into harmful actions. Prior empirical work documents hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures in LLMs that materially affect correctness in code and configuration settings [1],[2]. Architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures are proposed as mitigations, but published evaluations are typically prototype‑scale, offline, or vary in estimator semantics [3],[4],[5].

This paper reports a narrowly scoped, preregistered paired experiment (cand‑003‑stud‑001) that isolates the exact incremental effect of downstream deterministic validation and a single allowed repair call under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Under this design both baseline and guarded arms begin from the identical sampled initial candidate; any paired outcome difference must therefore arise solely from deterministic validator decisions and the permitted repair(s). Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact‑grounded paired experiment with full execution and deterministic reconciliation; (2) exact quantitative outcome reporting using the preregistered confirmatory test and preregistered descriptive summaries; and (3) an evidence‑grounded interpretation that reconciles preregistered power assumptions with observed high baseline validity and sparse repairs, clarifying what this estimand measures and does not measure. All preregistration, raw outputs, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution evidence bundle.
sections.related_work:
Surveys and controlled studies document LLM susceptibility to hallucination and prompt sensitivity that affect structured outputs, motivating verifier‑assisted pipelines in diverse domains [1],[2]. Constrained decoding and schema‑aware planning show measurable gains for executability in structured tasks, though primary evidence is often from non‑NetOps domains and gains depend on schema/tool fidelity [3],[4]. Recent NetOps and agentic‑AI system work emphasizes verifier‑assisted repair, guarded execution, and governance/proof‑carrying proposals; these works describe prototype improvements while underscoring dependence on validator coverage and protocol enforcement rather than any single model alone [5],[6],[7].

Our study complements these contributions by preregistering a paired estimand that, by design, measures only downstream validator/repair effects when the initial candidate is held constant. This avoids conflation with prompt/decoding interventions and provides a defined interpretable quantity useful for governance‑layer evaluation.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen design: The preregistration cand‑003‑stud‑001 was finalized and frozen before any model calls (preregistration_sha256 recorded in the execution manifest = ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec). Key preregistered elements: confirmatory paired binary design; task_count = 1000 deterministic tasks drawn from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one sampled initial generation per pair deterministically reused by both conditions); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar on the 2×2 paired contingency table. The preregistered power plan targeted an absolute effect of 0.15 assuming baseline≈0.60 (power >80% at two‑sided α = 0.05); that plan is recorded in the preregistration artifact and is discussed below with respect to observed baseline rates.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and analytic consequences: Under generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, baseline and guarded episodes reuse the same sampled candidate; the guarded pipeline may reject via deterministic validation and invoke at most one allowed repair. Paired differences therefore can only result from validator decisions and permitted repairs. The preregistration explicitly set independent_condition_generation = false; no independent first‑pass generations or constrained‑prompt arms were executed. Any post‑hoc interpretation invoking first‑pass prompt effects would contradict the frozen design.

Model and runtime configuration: The declared model was gpt‑5‑mini via provider openai_responses. The archived execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; validator/digital twin = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (version 5.0). The validator enforces workflow policies: required command presence and order (required_sequence), protected‑field noninterference, final_group_constraints, and returns a deterministic binary safe‑deploy verdict per task manifest.

Task corpus, sampling, and validator semantics: Tasks were selected deterministically using the registered ordinal rule from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 profile, producing 1000 unique tasks. Each task manifest records initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty label. The deterministic_netops_validator_v5 parses candidate command sequences, compares them to manifest constraints in a digital‑twin emulator, emits structured validator traces, and scores each episode with scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation producing a binary validity outcome archived per episode.

Execution constraints, retries, and missingness: The preregistered adapter limited retries (maximum_attempts_per_call = 1). The missingness_plan specified 'complete_pair_primary' treatment for incomplete pairs with a preregistered sensitivity treating failures as unsafe. Execution accounting is recorded in the manifest; provider call audit and stage_counts described in Results were produced automatically and are archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact‑grounded): The run started 2026‑09‑01T06:31:07Z and completed 2026‑09‑01T08:38:57Z. Planned episodes = 2000; completed = 2000; complete_pairs = 1000; failed episodes = 0. Provider call audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json): hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0; cache_miss_count = 1005. Stage counts record shared_initial_generation = 1000 and repair = 5. All deterministic consistency checks passed and cross‑condition cache reuse was not observed.

Primary paired outcomes and preregistered inferential test: The 2×2 paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered primary confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) returns p = 0.0625; this does not meet preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05, so preregistered H1 is not supported.

Preregistered secondary descriptive summaries and sensitivity: The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) yields [0.001, 0.01] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). The bootstrap interval excludes zero because bootstrap resampling with extremely sparse discordant counts can produce nonzero percentile bounds; this summary was preregistered as descriptive only. A one‑sided McNemar (guarded > baseline) produces p = 0.03125; because a one‑sided McNemar was not prespecified in cand‑003‑stud‑001 it is explicitly reported here as exploratory/post‑hoc.

Repair mechanics and representative traces: Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred (repair stage_count = 5). Representative episode artifacts (execution/scoring/task‑00000*.json) show validator rejection due to required_sequence violations or protected_interface touches, the adapter invoking the single allowed repair call, and validator acceptance of the repaired candidate after revalidation. All raw responses, provider call traces, repair traces (where present), and validator traces are archived and referenced in the deterministic_reconciliation and execution manifests.

Contamination, exclusions, and missingness: The preregistered contamination checks flagged no prompt leakage; contamination_summary.csv is empty. Missingness_summary.csv reports zero failed or unscorable episodes. No post‑hoc exclusions were applied. All seeds and task_index selection rules were fixed pre‑execution per the preregistration.

Interpretive accounting: Total model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). The small number of repairs constrains mechanistic inference about repair efficacy across failure modes and explains why discordant counts are sparse and discrete conditional tests have limited sensitivity to very small absolute improvements when baseline validity is near unity.
sections.discussion:
Confirmatory vs descriptive outcomes and preregistration fidelity: The preregistered primary inference is the exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625); preregistered H1 is therefore not supported at two‑sided α = 0.05. The paired bootstrap CI ([0.001, 0.01]) is a preregistered descriptive summary and excludes zero due to bootstrap sensitivity with sparse discordant pairs; this descriptive statistic does not override the preregistered confirmatory result. The one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was not prespecified in cand‑003‑stud‑001 and is explicitly labeled exploratory/post‑hoc; the preregistration artifact path and checksum are recorded in the execution manifest for verification.

Power assumption mismatch and consequences: The preregistered power_and_precision_plan assumed baseline ≈0.60 and targeted an absolute increase of 0.15 to achieve >80% power. The observed baseline success rate (0.995) is far higher than that assumption; this mismatch substantially reduces the study's sensitivity to detect small absolute gains because near‑unity baselines yield very few discordant pairs. The preregistered power calculation therefore does not apply to the observed data regime; this explains the inconclusive two‑sided McNemar despite a nonzero paired difference and motivates follow‑ups with tasks or models that produce higher baseline failure prevalence.

Mechanistic implications within shared_initial_candidate semantics: Because both arms reused the same sampled candidate, only downstream validation and permitted repairs can create differences. The five repairs demonstrate that a deterministic validator with suitable coverage can correct some required_sequence or protected-field violations. However, the low repair invocation count may reflect (a) relatively few initial candidate violations in the synthetic corpus, (b) generator behavior for the chosen model+prompt producing valid candidates, or (c) validator coverage that does not capture other semantic error classes. Distinguishing these mechanisms requires follow‑ups varying generator semantics, repair budgets, and validator rule sets.

Threats to validity and external generalization: Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 rule coverage; omissions in the validator's rule set could overestimate safety. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics correctly isolate downstream effects but preclude measuring prompt/decoding interventions. External validity: the synthetic corpus and single model (gpt‑5‑mini) limit generalization to heterogeneous production environments and other model families. Conclusion validity: sparse discordant counts limit power for detecting small absolute improvements; the preregistered power plan targeted a different baseline regime.

Operational implications and recommended follow‑ups grounded in artifacts: Artifact‑grounded evidence shows verifier‑guided repair can avert some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflows, but marginal gains depend on baseline failure prevalence, validator sensitivity, and permitted repair budget. Recommended preregistered follow‑ups (to be frozen before execution and archived) include: (1) independent first‑pass generation arms (no shared_initial_candidate) to measure prompt/decoding intervention effects; (2) repair budget sweeps (0..k repairs) to quantify marginal returns by failure class; (3) expanded validator suites and topology heterogeneity to probe external validity; and (4) evaluation across multiple model families. Each follow‑up should include a power plan aligned to realistic baseline rates and preregistered analysis choices.
sections.conclusion:
In a preregistered paired study with shared_initial_candidate semantics on a 1000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total model calls used = 1005. The primary inferential outcome remains the preregistered exact McNemar result; a one‑sided McNemar reported here (p = 0.03125) was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration and is presented as exploratory/post‑hoc. These artifact‑grounded results indicate that downstream verifier/repair safeguards can prevent some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflows, but measurable marginal gains are constrained when baseline outputs are already highly valid and when the paired design intentionally isolates downstream effects. All preregistration, execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived with the run to support reproducibility and to guide preregistered follow‑ups that broaden model diversity, validator coverage, and repair budgets.

limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch is reported explicitly and reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
